about: The named edits that turn today's elevation data into the island of 1628 BCE (work order 001). Each edit carries its claim references (lane#row, as corrected in docs/research/verification/) or a liberty number (T-L…, listed in docs/terrain/README.md), and its parameters. A later research result changes a number here, not the code in build.mjs. All positions are [x, z] in metres from 36.405 N, 25.405 E (x east, z south); heights are metres above the sea level of 1628 BCE.

E0.name: Surface-model clean-up
E0.note: GLO-30 is a surface model: buildings stand in it. Inside these town outlines a 3x3 morphological opening at the source resolution removes narrow highs. Vegetation on Santorini is low and is not treated.

E1.name: Sea level
E1.note: Regional value for the northern and central Cyclades, c. 2000 BC to c. 30 BC: 3.60 +/- 0.20 m below present (T1#51, T1#52), which includes a local tectonic part of 1-1.2 m. The alternative, recorded beside it, is an older Aegean-wide estimate of less than 0.5 m below present (T1c#37). Neither is measured on Santorini, whose own vertical movement is unknown (T1c sea-level note), so the choice is a liberty (T-L13). The join of the two datasets' height references (EGM2008 for the land, lowest astronomical tide for the sea floor) is made with no offset, also a liberty (T1c correction 12).

E2.name: Remove the Kameni islands
E2.note: They formed after the eruption. Everything inside this outline, above and below the water, is replaced by the bay floor (E5) or by restored land (E4). The published volumes (4.85 +/- 0.7 km3 DRE for all products; 3.2 km3 for the islands) are different measures and are not used as parameters (T1 correction 8).

E3.name: Strip the Minoan eruption deposits from the land
E3.note: No thickness map could be opened (T1c gap): the figures are thicknesses at named places, and the surface built from them is a liberty. The model: thickest along the caldera rim (the whole pile reaches about 55 m at the caldera wall and about 40 m on the rim: T1c#1, #7) and in the coastal fans (up to 40 m: T1c#8, #9); close to nothing on the outer flanks of Profitis Ilias, Mikro Profitis Ilias and Megalo Vouno (T1c#11, correction 5) and on west Akrotiri around Loumarades and Kokkino Vouno (T1c#12); elsewhere thin on ridges and steep slopes and thicker in hollows. Never more than 55 m, the most reported for the whole pile (T1c#1, correction 1; another source gives 50 m, recorded as the alternative), and never enough to move the coast (the pre-eruption coastline is not known). The mean on land comes out near the 17 m that the published volumes imply (T1c#19, an inference). Mavrorachidi's ~25 m is depth to bedrock at one core and is not used (T1 correction 1).

zones.name: Megalo Vouno and Mikro Profitis Ilias, upper ground
West Akrotiri: Loumarades and Kokkino Vouno
Southern and south-eastern fan, to Vlychada

atTown.name: The deposits over the town of Akrotiri, as first reported
atTown.note: A 1978 conference report, its author unnamed for these figures: a fall of fine pumice of about 1-2 cm, then an ash fall of about 1-2 m over the town, then the main pumice as a base surge. It is recorded here and not used: it conflicts with today's description of metres of first-phase pumice, so it does not set a strip depth (T1c correction 2). build.mjs reports what the model strips at the town site (E8) so the two can be read side by side.

E3.zonesNote: Each zone: "metres" sets the thickness there, "scale" multiplies the model, "aboveMetres" limits it to higher ground.

E4.name: Restore the ring island on the caldera side
E4.note: The southern part of today's caldera, and the south-western gaps between Thera, Aspronisi and Therasia, were land. The restored surface is modelled: a membrane stretched between the surviving land around it, a rim crest and an outer coast, with an inner wall falling to the bay. The rim crest reaches about 260 m (T1b#51, preferred value). The volume added must fall within 9.1-17.1 km3 (T1#14); build.mjs reports it and fails outside that range. The source measures that range as the volume between its restored surface and today's surface, sea floor included (T1 verification, addendum of 2026-11-18, from the full paper), which is how build.mjs measures it. Within the range the source prefers the upper end (17.1 km3, the largest land that fits: its rim at 260 m, the smallest bay, only the cliffs known to predate the eruption left untouched) and gives a separate estimate of 14.4 +/- 0.8 km3 from the rock fragments in the eruption deposits; the 9.1 km3 end it calls less realistic. Work order 004 (D29) raised the volume from 13.16 km3 towards those figures: see fromTheBay, rimCrest, rimMaxMetres and erosion below, and docs/terrain/README.md.
E4.fromTheBayNote: Work order 004 (D29). Two more pieces of today's caldera are land: its south-east corner below Thera's wall, and its south-west corner below Therasia's southern cape. Each outline is southLand's old north edge and the new shore of the bay. The source's preferred reconstruction has the smallest bay that leaves the cliffs known to predate the eruption untouched (T1#14, addendum). On the Thera side the bay still reaches 1.0 km south of the latitude of Fira, whose harbour wall predates the eruption (T1#19), and ends 2.4 km north of Athinios (T1#20); before, 1.7 km and 1.7 km. The new shore is nowhere nearer to Pre-Kameni (E7, unchanged) than the old shore was at its nearest (709 m, in the middle of the south shore, which did not move): that island's place is what stops the bay from being made smaller still. Where the new land meets Thera's wall and Therasia's cape, the cliff that no longer faces the bay is covered up to its top, as southLand already did further south (those cliffs are fresh, cut by the eruption: T1c#24). The line of the new shore is a liberty (T-L2, T-L3).
E4.rimCrestNote: About 500 m inland of the bay's shore all the way round. 260 m along the restored arc (T1b#51), coming down only to meet the surviving land at each end: Thera's rim, about 195 m here once E3 has stripped it, and Therasia's southern ridge, about 150 m. Before work order 004 it reached 260 m at one point and stood at 205-255 m elsewhere, and the gullies then cut it down to 251 m at most.

erosion.note: Work order 004. The gullies are cut into the smooth restored surface, which is the kind of surface the source's volume is measured on. Cut that way they removed 1.0 km3 of the 14.2 km3 the smooth surface held, and lowered the rim crest by 9 m. giveBack is the share of what they remove that is given back as a broad swell under them (a blur over giveBackWindowMetres), so that ridges stand above the smooth surface and gullies below it; rimKeepMetres is how far from the rim crest the gullies begin, so that the crest keeps its sourced height. Both are liberties (T-L2).

E5.name: The northern bay
E5.note: A flooded caldera in the north part of today's caldera only, shallow and lagoonal: all of today's caldera water (and the Kameni islands, E2) that can be reached from the seed without crossing E4's restored land or E6's low ground. Its north, north-east and east walls are today's cliffs, which largely predate the eruption (T1#4, T1#19); it reaches south to below Fira harbour (T1#19) and stops north of Athinios (T1#20). 'No more than a few metres' deep is T1b#46 (B, to verify, and contested); the depth, the outline of the south shore and the keeping of Therasia's east cliffs as the west wall are liberties.

E6.name: The opening to the sea
E6.note: At most a narrow, low channel to the north or north-west. Today's 1 km wide strait between Thera and Therasia was cut by the sea flooding in after the eruption (T1#10), so it is filled back to low land (counted in the E4 volume) and a channel is left through it. The channel's width (under 1 km, today's width being the upper bound), depth and course, and the height of the low ground beside it, are liberties.

E7.name: Pre-Kameni, the island in the bay (a modern label)
E7.note: A low dome of about 2.4 km3 (the DEM value) of black glassy andesite, with the first-phase vent of the eruption on it, 1-2 km west of modern Fira. No height or footprint is published. The shape here is a liberty: an elliptical dome h = H(1 - r^p), its summit kept below the 260 m rim (the shield-scaled heights of 340-420 m would stand above it). Volume = pi a b H p/(p+2). No buildings: no source supports them (T1b gap; T1b-4).

E8.name: Akrotiri and the south coast
E8.note: The town site (the modern excavation, about 1 km south of today's caldera edge) gets a gently sloping terrace for work order 002: a small rise at about 20-25 m (T1#35, B, to verify) falling gently to the sea. Its exact form is a liberty. The harbour has not been found (T1#36, T1#37): one view puts it in an embayment between Mesovouna and Mavro Rachidi south of the site (T1c#17, #34), another still places an eastern harbour at Potamos, where seismics found no bay (T1c#16, T1c correction 4). So the coast is left as the data and E3 give it: no harbour is cut.

ridge.note: Work order 002 reshaped the terrace for the town. The town grew along the crest of a ridge running north to south, with Complex Delta's west house on the crest and a steep fall to the east at Xeste 4 (T2b#37, T2b#38: grade A that the ridge and the fall exist). The crest here runs due north-south through the middle of the excavated walls; the ground is level for crestHalfWidthMetres on each side of it and then falls away, easing in over easeMetres, never by more than maxFallMetres. North of the excavated town the fall dies out (fadesBetweenZ: none north of the first z, all of it south of the second), because the town is drawn running on over a plateau there (T2b#67, grade C). The 40 m grid cannot hold a sheer slope: the fall at Xeste 4 is far gentler here than the excavator describes. Every number in this block is a liberty (T-L6).

sourcedLevels.note: The two levels a source gives, both above today's sea; E1's sea-level change is added to compare them with the model. They guide hillTopMetres and slopeTowardsSea; they are not forced. No street gradient is measured (T2b verification, Gaps), so the 3.5% fall along the crest is a liberty (T-L6), chosen so that streets drain towards the sea (T2#11, T2#12).

xeste3.grade: A (the excavator's "elevation"; above sea level is implied)

eastEdge.what: the floor of a part-basement room at the east end of the excavation, beside Xeste 2; the room stood about 1 m above the road, so the road lay above this floor

E9.name: Profitis Ilias
E9.note: The old non-volcanic basement keeps its shape; E3 strips almost nothing here. The 30 m data reads both summits several metres low, so they are raised to their published heights (grade B: no survey is named; T1c correction 3): Profitis Ilias 565 m (T1c#53; the data's highest cell is 560.4 m, T1c#54) and Mesa Vouno 369 m (359.9 m in the data). Heights are above today's sea level; E1 then adds the sea-level change.

rock.name: Rock classes
rock.note: 0 undivided volcanic rocks of the ring (default); 1 light-grey andesite, Akrotiri peninsula (T1#23); 2 dark-grey andesite, Therasia (T1#23); 3 black glassy andesite, Pre-Kameni (T1b#43); 4 phyllite and schist basement (T1#21); 5 marble (T1b#56); 6 the floor of the bay, shown as pale sediment (T1#12: aragonite buildups and shallow-marine, lagoonal life in the bay; its colour is a liberty). The claims name places, not boundaries: every outline here is a liberty. Athinios (T1#21) is not drawn: its basement crops out in the caldera wall that the eruption exhumed (T1#20), which in 1628 BCE lay under the restored land.
